agree.reason: The plain apology, its real cause and the dated commitment to January 7 answer the cold email directly, and the asks are small and concrete, so this investor would probably take the call, though nothing yet shows the company getting out of a flat quarter.

honest.reason: Every figure matches the facts, the 11-month runway is correct arithmetic, and the risk from the records system is stated without softening; the only claim not in the brief is the plain definition of a no-show.

works_the_facts.reason: Runway is worked out, but the writer leaves other easy figures unworked: the lost chain was about 13% of MRR, the $3,800 at risk is about 9%, the six reminder commitments add about $900 a month, the no-show rate nearly halved, and the cash runs out around October 2027.

right_comparison.reason: The competing records-system schedulers are described honestly, but the draft never sets out what happens if the current trend holds (flat MRR, a steady $44k burn, cash gone by roughly autumn 2027) against what the reminder product might change.

qualification.reason: The uncertainty about who will buy reminders comes with a checkable date (January 7), and the at-risk accounts carry a dollar figure, but neither has a threshold or a stated consequence, such as what follows if fewer than six clinics buy at launch or if the two accounts leave.

objections.reason: It meets the main objection, the silence, head-on with a cause and a commitment, and it raises the churn risk before the investor can, but it leaves out the likely next question about fundraising or extending runway while the right to join the next round is in play.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured investor email of about 470 words, under the 500 limit, though the sign-off still reads '[Your name]' when the writer knew it was Sam Patel.
